narr: Welcome to Weeks 5 through 7 of English for Engineering. In this section, we'll focus on grammar exercises related to passive voice in different tenses.
Let's begin with Week 5 Grammar Worksheet exercises.

data.heading: Exercise 1 — Past Simple Passive
data.problem: Complete the sentence with the past simple passive form of the verb in brackets.

steps.text: In ancient times, fires (light) were lit to use smoke as a signal over long distances.
Morse code (invent) ___ by an American called Samuel Morse.
The world's first television images (show) ___ to scientists in Scotland in 1926.
Radios (use) ___ to broadcast coded messages during the Second World War.
The World Wide Web (design) ___ originally to make it easier for nuclear physics researchers to communicate.
Buying books and CDs over the Internet (make) ___ popular by the company Amazon.

narr: Our first exercise focuses on the past simple passive tense.
For each sentence, we need to complete it with the correct past simple passive form of the verb in brackets.
Remember that the past simple passive uses 'was' or 'were' followed by the past participle of the main verb.

data.heading: Exercise 1 — Past Simple Passive (cont.)

steps.text: The first mobile phones with cameras (sell) ___ in Japan.
Vinyl albums and tapes (replace) ___ by CDs, which are now being replaced by mp3.
The first English dictionary (wrote) ___ by Robert Cawdrey in 1604.
The first mass-produced cars (introduce) ___ by the Ford company in the USA.

data.result: Answer: (b) was invented; (c) were shown; (d) were used; (e) was designed; (f) was made; (g) were sold; (h) were replaced; (i) was written — the worksheet gives the past form wrote, but the passive needs the past participle written; (j) were introduced. Every sentence describes a finished past event, so the form is was/were + past participle (Rule 6).

narr: Let's look at the answers now.

data.heading: Exercise 2 — How a Toy Car is Made (Present Simple Passive)
data.problem: Read the text and underline all the subject, verb and object structures. Then rewrite the text using present simple passive verbs. Leave out any unnecessary words.

steps.text: As a first step, a computer is used to plan the exact shape of the car.
In the factory, they use a computer to plan the exact shape of the car. They then feed this computer program into a machine, and produce a plastic prototype.
Then they produce the actual toy cars in a factory abroad.
As far as construction is concerned, they make the bodies of the cars from plastic.
They add small electric motors to the cars, and then they paint them. They also attach licence plates.
Quality control inspects the cars and then they wrap them and pack them into cardboard boxes.
They ship the cars to Britain.

data.result: Answer: (a) As a first step, a computer is used to plan the exact shape of the car. (given) (b) This computer program is then fed into a machine, and a plastic prototype is produced. (c) The actual toy cars are produced in a factory abroad. (d) The bodies of the cars are made from plastic (as far as construction is concerned). (e) Small electric motors are added to the cars, and then they are painted; licence plates are also attached. (f) At the next stage, the cars are inspected by quality control, and then they are wrapped and packed into cardboard boxes. (g) Finally, the cars are shipped to Britain. The first words of items c-g are printed in the worksheet; item b, partly hidden in the scan, is reconstructed in the same pattern. The general subjects they are left out because they are unnecessary (Rule 2c).

narr: Now let's move to Exercise 2, which focuses on the present simple passive.
This exercise asks us to rewrite a text about how a toy car is made using present simple passive verbs.
The key here is to identify the subject, verb, and object structures in the original text and then transform them into passive voice.
Remember that in present simple passive, we use 'is' or 'are' followed by the past participle of the main verb.
Let's examine the answers to this exercise.

data.heading: Exercise 3 — The Freedom Ship (Will Passive or Present Perfect Passive)
data.problem: Complete the text with either the will passive or present perfect passive forms of the verbs in brackets.

steps.text: In recent years many plans (make) have been made for large floating cities with living accommodation for as many as 50,000 people.
One such project which b (advertise) ___ is the Freedom Ship.
According to the plans for this project, this huge ship c (construct) ___ from smaller units, which d (take) ___ out to sea for final assembly.
The ship e (power) ___ by 100 diesel engines, and the residents on board f (carry) ___ around the world continuously.
The large number of people on the ship g (provide) ___ with all kinds of food, entertainment and sports facilities, and modern recycling methods h (use) ___ to save energy on board.
At the time of writing, this project i (not build) ___, and j (criticize) ___ by some people who say it is too expensive.
We shall have to wait and see whether this ambitious plan ever becomes reality.

data.result: Answer: (b) has been advertised; (c) will be constructed; (d) will be taken; (e) will be powered; (f) will be carried; (g) will be provided; (h) will be used; (i) has not been built; (j) has been criticized. The plans that already exist at the time of writing take the present perfect passive; everything that will happen once the ship is built takes the will passive.

narr: Exercise 3 introduces a more complex concept using either will passive or present perfect passive.
This exercise is about the Freedom Ship project, and we need to determine which form of passive voice is appropriate for each blank.
Remember that present perfect passive is used for actions that have been completed recently or have relevance to the present, while will passive is used for future actions.
Let's look at the answers to understand how to choose between these two forms.

data.heading: Exercise 4 — Present Perfect Passive with By
data.problem: Rewrite the sentence using a present perfect passive with by. Leave out any unnecessary words.

steps.text: Cheaper air travel has made possible the global expansion in tourism. →The global expansion in tourism has been made possible by cheaper air travel.
Countries all over the world have experienced a growth in tourism.
Millions of tourists have visited the popular Mediterranean resorts since the 1970s.
Recently tourists have chosen more distant locations in Africa, Asia and South America.
Mass tourism has badly affected some countries.
International companies have built large hotels on unspoilt coastline.
These developments have disturbed local wildlife.

data.result: Answers would follow the pattern shown in item a, transforming each sentence into present perfect passive with 'by' phrase.

narr: Our final exercise focuses on transforming sentences into present perfect passive with 'by' phrases.
This helps emphasize the doer of the action in passive constructions.
The pattern is: subject + has/have been + past participle + by + doer of the action.
Let's consider how we would transform each sentence following this pattern.

data.heading: Summary of Passive Voice Constructions
items: Past Simple Passive: was/were + past participle
Present Simple Passive: is/are + past participle
Will Passive: will be + past participle
Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + past participle

narr: Throughout these exercises, we've explored different forms of the passive voice in English.
Each form serves specific purposes and time references.
Mastering these constructions is essential for clear technical communication in engineering contexts.
